matches.text: An inventory taken on gaining possession was concerned primarily with record- ing the state of the house and of the fixtures; it is as likely as not to be in narrative form, as was the view of Petworth when the eighth Earl of Northumberland came to take possession in 1574 after his brother’s execution *. A list was generally made of the fixtures in each room, with or, more usually, without their value; an inventory of Syon House in 1593 lists as fixtures ‘ plate locks, stocklocks, <IA_FTS_MATCH>glass</IA_FTS_MATCH>, bars of iron, bolts, handles, mattings, iron casements, wooden casements, wainscot shuttings, sheets of lead, cisterns of lead, cocks, dresser boards, tables, forms, tressels, and cupboards, with doors and iron work unto them belonging’. Occasionally, a plan of the house was attached to this type of inventory, often with no more than the barest indication of the size of the main wings °.

In editing the manuscripts, the recommendations of the Report on Editing Historical Documents in the Bulletin of the Institute of Historical Research, i (1925), 6-25, have been borne in mind. The spelling of the MSS. has been retained, but the initial ff has been rendered F or f, as the sense required, and abbreviations the mean- ing of which is undoubted have been extended, except that common abbreviations used for money, weights and measures have been retained. Figures, numerals and the abbreviations for quarter and farthing, however, have been standardized; quarter appears as gir. and farthing as guaz. Abbreviations of which the meaning is in the least uncertain have been extendedand the extensions placed between square brackets. Capitals and punctuation have been modernized and the text as far as possible paragraphed, to make for easier <IA_FTS_MATCH>reading</IA_FTS_MATCH> and printing. Where bracketing in the accounts has extended over more than one sub-heading’s entry for the purpose of summing, the extent of the bracketing has been indicated by the insertion in italics of capital letters against the first and last figures and of the word ‘ Total’ at the end. All editorial insertions appear in square brackets and in italics; textual notes are indicated by superior small letters and editorial notes by superior small numerals. The annotations do not, as a rule, include elucidations which are given in the Glossary or Index. The physical appearance of the MSS. is illustrated by the plates and described in Section II of the Introduction; ‘ Aln. MSS.’ refers to the Duke of North- umberland’s Alnwick Castle MSS., “Syon MSS.’ to his Grace’s Syon House MSS., and ‘ S.H.MSS.’ to those of his Grace’s Syon House MSS. which are now at Alnwick Castle, Northumberand. The reference ‘ MSS.’ indicates that more than one docu- ment is contained in the box or volume bearing the number quoted.

1 Bedford sacs Wa town house of the Earls of Bedford, was on the north side of the Strand, on the site of the present Southampton Street; Boswell House was on the site of the Law Courts in Carey Street and was rented from a Mr Ralph Boswell or Bosvile from the spring of 1586; and a house at Tottenham had been hired for } yr. to Lady Day, 1586. In the MS., Tottenham is usually rendered Totnam; the spelling has been consistently expanded for convenience of <IA_FTS_MATCH>reading</IA_FTS_MATCH>.
